opportunities.title: Synthesis grants

amount.raw: Synthesis groups can claim up to £30,000 over two years for groups of 8-15 participants.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Main applicant must have BES membership; groups of 8-15 individuals with diverse mix of career stages, institutions and international participation; not required for all group members to be members.
opportunities.summary: Fast-tracking innovative and impactful research by contributing up to £30k towards the formation of new two-year synthesis groups that bring together diverse interdisciplinary groups to analyse and synthesise existing data.

opportunities.title: Long-term research grants

amount.raw: You will be able to claim the first five years' worth of funding in year 1, which is £3,500... in the sixth year, you can claim an additional £3,500. Averages £500 a year for a decade.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners, reserve managers, consultants and university academics; awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Provides funding over 10 years for long-term ecological studies anywhere in the world, funding the annual cost of a few days of data gathering over a long period, enabling existing short-term projects with 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical research and development grants

amount.raw: Projects can be awarded up to £5,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level (early years to life-long learning, formal or informal settings); awarded to individuals, not organisations; projects max 12 months.
opportunities.summary: Improving the education of future generations of ecologists by providing up to £5k towards evidence-based learning, funding research on education methods within ecology to inform teaching and learning practices.

opportunities.title: Connecting ecologists with other disciplines grants

amount.raw: Grant awards of up to £20,000 can be claimed from the applicant.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership; open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations; undergraduates and masters students not eligible; awarded to individuals, not organisations; placements up to 12 months.
opportunities.summary: Promoting interdisciplinary skills by funding up to £20k towards placements in different disciplines and sectors, immersing an ecologist in another professional world where ecology can make a difference.

opportunities.title: Small research grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: BES membership required; funding for researchers from all countries globally; projects can be conducted anywhere in the world; not a scholarship; will not fund projects forming part of a funded fellowship or completion of an undergraduate/master's degree.
opportunities.summary: Providing up to £5,000 for new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard, supporting projects with a clear ecological science focus.

opportunities.title: Outreach and engagement grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership; open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels; no restrictions on where applicants come from or carry out work; projects max 12 months.
opportunities.summary: Providing funding of up to £2,000 for individuals, teams and organisations to engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science through outreach, public engagement and science communication activities.

opportunities.title: Training and travel grants

amount.raw: A maximum of £250 is available to cover registration fees for virtual conferences/courses; a maximum of £500 is available for events in person.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member; must be a PhD student or postgraduate researcher (postdoc researchers, undergraduates and masters students not eligible); work/study at a university or research institution; work in scientific areas within the remit of ecology.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses and the travel costs associated with presenting their work at workshops and conferences.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any career stage; must be a citizen of and based in the Global South; must be travelling from and returning to the Global South country; must have applied to present at the Annual Meeting; must be at least three years since last awarded a BES Training and Travel Grant.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting in the UK, covering travel, registration, food and accommodation costs up to £1,000.
